Problem Statement
Problem: Graph Theory - 16
Prove that any k-chromatic graph admits an orientation in which a longest directed path
consists of exactly k vertices.
1
proof_numbered:
0001 | Solution:
0002 | Theorem 1. Any k-chromatic graph G admits an orientation in which a longest
0003 | directed path consists of exactly k vertices.
0004 | Proof. We prove this result through the following steps:
0005 | Lemma 2. Every k-chromatic graph G has a k-critical subgraph H.
0006 | Proof. If G is already k-critical, we take H = G. Otherwise, G has a vertex v
0007 | such that G −v is still k-chromatic. We iteratively remove such vertices until
0008 | we obtain a k-critical subgraph H.
0009 | Lemma 3. In any k-critical graph H, δ(H) ≥k −1 where δ denotes the mini-
0010 | mum degree.
0011 | Proof. If there exists a vertex v with d(v) < k −1, then H −v can be properly
0012 | colored with k−1 colors (since H is k-critical), and we can extend this coloring to
0013 | v (since v has at most k−2 neighbors), contradicting that H is k-chromatic.
0014 | Now proceed with the main proof:
0015 | 1. Let G be a k-chromatic graph. By the first lemma, it contains a k-critical
0016 | subgraph H.
0017 | 2. By the second lemma, δ(H) ≥k −1. Thus H has a vertex vk of degree
0018 | at least k −1.
0019 | 3. Since H is k-critical, H −vk is (k −1)-colorable. Let V1, . . . , Vk−1 be the
0020 | color classes in some proper (k −1)-coloring of H −vk.
0021 | 4. Add vk to form Vk = {vk}, creating a partition V1, . . . , Vk.
0022 | 5. Orient the edges of H as follows:
0023 |  For edges between different Vi and Vj with i < j, orient from Vi to Vj
0024 |  For edges within the same Vi, orient arbitrarily
0025 | 6. This orientation is acyclic because:
0026 |  Any directed cycle would require both an edge from Vi to Vj and from Vj
0027 | to Vi with i ̸= j, which is impossible
0028 |  Within each Vi, edges are oriented arbitrarily but cannot form cycles since
0029 | Vi is an independent set in H −vk and Vk is a single vertex
0030 | 7. The longest directed path in this orientation:
0031 |  Must have vertices in distinct Vi’s (since edges only go from lower to higher
0032 | indexed partitions)
0033 |  Can have at most k vertices (one from each Vi)
0034 |  Achieves exactly k vertices: Start with a neighbor of vk in Vk−1, then a
0035 | neighbor of that vertex in Vk−2, and so on, building a path backwards
0036 | through the partitions until reaching V1, then ending at vk
0037 | 2
0038 | 
0039 | 8.
0040 | Extend this orientation to all of G by orienting any additional edges
0041 | arbitrarily (these cannot create longer paths since H already contains a k-vertex
0042 | path and no longer path exists in H).
0043 | Thus we have constructed an orientation of G where the longest directed
0044 | path has exactly k vertices.
